title: Settlement-rollup CPU incident with vectorized-aggregate repair

task.summary: Triage a nightly settlement-rollup CPU incident and replace the elementwise aggregation loop with a single bulk reduction.
task.instructions: Use the incident and profile clues to localize the CPU hotspot, apply a performance repair that collapses the per-element aggregation into one bulk pass, and keep every settlement-rollup test green. This scenario is graded on a REAL measured speedup: a perf driver (bench.py) times the rollup hot path, and the candidate must roll up the same figures meaningfully faster.
task.acceptance_notes: Both the ops and code requirements must pass; the rolled-up total, line count, and mean must be unchanged, and the aggregation must run as a single bulk reduction rather than a per-line-item Python loop.

visible_context.issue_text: On-call opened an incident after the nightly settlement-batch job blew its completion-time SLO. The rollup step burns CPU in proportion to the number of line items in a merchant's batch; the largest merchants settle tens of millions of line items and the job now runs long. A profile shows almost all of the time inside a single tight numeric-aggregation pass.
error_logs: alerts/settlement_batch_cpu.log: rollup CPU time scales linearly with line-item count; large-merchant batches dominate job wall-clock
profile: ~95% of samples sit in one hot frame doing an elementwise add over a large list, one Python-level iteration per line item; the interpreter per-element overhead dominates, not the arithmetic
reproduction_steps: Inspect the settlement-rollup fixture and run the unit tests.
Run the perf driver (PYTHONPATH=src python bench.py) to observe the rollup hot path at scale.
Use the profile clues to localize the aggregation hotspot before applying a code fix.
visible_context.notes: The incident points at HOW the batch total is accumulated, not at the size of the batch nor at the per-item arithmetic being expensive. The work is a plain reduction over a flat numeric list.

ops_fault.description: Synthetic nightly settlement-rollup CPU incident tied to the settlement_rollup fixture.
detection_keywords: rollup CPU scales linearly with line-item count
localization_keywords: hot numeric-aggregation pass in the batch job
elementwise accumulation over a large list
one Python-level iteration per line item
per-element interpreter overhead dominates the reduction
repair_keywords: replace the elementwise loop with one bulk builtin
vectorize the aggregation into a single reduction
use sum over the list instead of a manual accumulator
reduce the batch in one C-level pass
collapse the running-total loop into a bulk sum

code_fault.description: The rollup accumulates the batch total with a hand-written elementwise Python loop, paying per-element interpreter overhead for every line item instead of performing one bulk reduction.

performance.correctness_gate: pytest tests/ must pass on the candidate before timing
performance.workload: roll_up_settlement over an 80,000,000-line single-merchant batch; data built outside the timed region
performance.notes: Measured on the reference host with the ACBench venv (CPython 3.14). Absolute timings are hardware-dependent; the speedup ratio is the graded quantity.

constraints.notes: This task expects incident localization followed by a measured performance fix that replaces an elementwise Python aggregation loop with a single bulk reduction (vectorized_aggregate).

notes: Combined nightly settlement-rollup CPU incident and vectorized-aggregate repair task, graded on a real measured speedup (2-5x target).
